segments.text: It is shaped like an arrowhead — a pentagonal structure with a pointed end aimed toward the southwest and a broad, flat back facing the northeast.

segments.text: These interior spaces have led some researchers to call Building J an observatory — a building designed to channel light from specific astronomical events into specific interior positions, allowing priests to track the movements of stars and planets.

segments.text: This is a convention found across Mesoamerican writing systems: a hill glyph with distinguishing features means "this place." Above or beside the hill sign, there is often an upside-down human head with closed eyes.

segments.text: The meaning is stark: this place was conquered, and its leader was killed.
segments.text_markdown: The meaning is stark: this place was conquered, and its leader was killed.
segments.title: Chapter 6 — Building J and the Conquest Slabs

tts.text: Betydelsen är tydlig: denna plats erövrades, och dess ledare dödades.

segments.text: Additional glyphs on each slab provide what appear to be the name of the place and, in some cases, calendrical information — perhaps the date of the conquest.

segments.text: Caso called these "conquest slabs," and his interpretation has largely held up over ninety years of subsequent research.

segments.text: Building J, in this reading, is a victory monument — a three-dimensional record of every place Monte Albán claimed to have subdued, carved in stone and displayed at the very center of the city's most important public space.
segments.text_markdown: Building J, in this reading, is a victory monument — a three-dimensional record of every place Monte Albán claimed to have subdued, carved in stone and displayed at the very center of the city's most important public space.

tts.text: Byggnad Jay är, enligt denna tolkning, ett segermonument — en tredimensionell uppteckning av varje plats Monte Albán hävdade att ha underkuvat, ristad i sten och utställd i stadens viktigaste offentliga rums absoluta centrum.

segments.text: The political purpose is clear enough.
segments.text_markdown: The political purpose is clear enough.

tts.text: Det politiska syftet är tydligt nog.

segments.text: A visitor arriving at Monte Albán for the first time — a trader from the coast, a diplomat from a neighboring valley, a newly conquered tributary — would have walked into the Grand Plaza and seen Building J at its center, covered with carved records of Monte Albán's military victories.

segments.text: The message would have been impossible to miss: this city conquers.

tts.text: Erövringsplattorna skryter inte bara om våld.

segments.text: They record specific places, with identifiable place names, on a permanent public monument.

segments.title: Chapter 6 — Building J and the Conquest Slabs

tts.text: De registrerar specifika platser, med identifierbara ortnamn, på ett permanent offentligt monument.

segments.text: They are making a legal claim: these territories belong to us, and here is the proof.
segments.text_markdown: They are making a legal claim: these territories belong to us, and here is the proof.
segments.title: Chapter 6 — Building J and the Conquest Slabs

tts.text: De gör ett juridiskt anspråk: dessa territorier tillhör oss, och här är beviset.

segments.text: It is not so different from the boundary stelae of Egyptian pharaohs or the triumphal arches of Roman emperors — a universal impulse to record and display military achievement, expressed in a distinctly Mesoamerican visual language.
